claim: communication.md section 4 quotes the HVR boundary explicitly: the full standard, including vocabulary and structural tells, lives in hvr-rules.md and is to be loaded when writing a document rather than a reply.
HVR is document-scoped by its own text: purpose is all documentation output, usage names document types, and its section 9 structure demands numbered ALL-CAPS H2s and dividers with no TOC.
HVR's voice directives and word/tell lists are modality-neutral and can bind a reply; communication.md already carries the punctuation subset for replies and points at HVR for the rest.

The correct treatment is to reach into HVR for the tells while communication.md keeps the reply, naming the applicable layers in the invoking mode contract; a boundary change is only needed if HVR must bind every reply, and then only to section 4's one-line load sentence.

The rule-versus-contract test: statements identical for every mode belong to reply doctrine; statements that vary by the mode's artifact belong to the mode contract, which is also the only artifact that loads at fan-out and non-interactive completion moments.

A repo rule restating the presentation obligation would duplicate communication.md sections 7 and 8, which the corpus's duplication guard forbids; the sibling packet 046 is the right owner because the missing content is per-mode field shape.
The test battery converges on deep-loop-contracts-only: Q1 passes trigger-shaped, Q2 passes In, Q3 refuses the new-file and in-place routes, Q4 locates the real failure in the presentation templates.

answer: HVR can bind a reply in part: voice directives and word/tell lists apply, the document-structure layer does not. The tells route is correct; the mode contracts should name the applicable subset. No boundary change needed for this case; only a universal reply-wide HVR grade would require amending section 4's one-line load sentence, which fits under the 250-line ceiling.

Rule binds cross-cutting reply posture (already in communication.md sections 2,5,6,7,8 and handoff-and-questions for the turn end); contract binds the mode's artifact and completion-message fields. Per-mode field lists in a rule would restate communication.md and duplicate the contracts, so the sibling packet 046 owns the change and the rule set needs no addition.
